note: Approved by the owner and frozen on 11 November 2026. 24 briefs, 6 of each kind. Used only to confirm a result that will change the system. Never used to write or adjust a prompt. No brief has a human reference text yet.

briefs.prompt: Write an explanation of about 300 words of why the sky is blue at midday and red at sunset. The reader is a curious twelve-year-old.
Write an explanation of about 800 words of how an mRNA vaccine prepares the immune system for a virus it has not met. The reader is an adult with no biology beyond school.
Write an explanation of about 1,000 words of how a central bank raising its interest rate is meant to bring inflation down. The reader is a general newspaper reader.
Write an explanation of about 600 words of how a satellite navigation receiver works out where it is. The reader is a general reader.
Write an explanation of about 500 words of how compound interest works and why the age at which someone starts saving for a pension matters. The reader is someone in their first job.
Write an explanation of about 2,000 words of how an electricity grid keeps supply and demand in balance from second to second. The reader is a general reader who follows the news about energy.
Write an opinion piece of about 800 words on whether a four-day working week should become the standard. Take a side and argue for it.
Write an essay of about 1,000 words on whether voting in national elections should be compulsory. Take a side and argue for it.
Write an opinion piece of about 600 words on whether every code change should need another engineer's approval before it is merged. Take a side and argue for it. The readers are working engineers.
Write an opinion piece of about 500 words on whether zoos should exist. Take a side and argue for it.
Write an essay of about 1,500 words on whether a company should require its staff to work from the office on set days. Take a side and argue for it. The readers are managers.
Write a letter to a newspaper of about 300 words on whether a city should charge drivers to enter its centre. Take a side and argue for it.
Write a narrative account of about 600 words of the collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in 1940. The reader is a general reader.
Write a narrative account of about 1,200 words of how penicillin went from Alexander Fleming's laboratory to mass production. The reader is a general reader.
Write a narrative account of about 2,000 words of Ernest Shackleton's Endurance expedition. The reader is a general reader.
Write a narrative account of about 800 words of the Great Fire of London in 1666. The reader is a general reader.
Write a narrative account of about 1,000 words of the Therac-25 radiation therapy accidents. The readers are software engineers.
Write a narrative account of about 500 words of John Harrison and the marine chronometer. The reader is a general reader.

Write a technical description of about 800 words of how a B-tree index speeds up a database query and what it costs on insert. The reader is a backend developer who writes SQL and has not studied database internals.
Write a technical description of about 1,000 words of how a generational garbage collector works. The reader is a developer who has only used languages with manual memory management.
Write a technical description of about 600 words of how a browser checks a website's certificate chain. The reader is a junior web developer.
Write a technical description of about 500 words of what a Linux container is and how it differs from a virtual machine. The reader is a developer who has used Docker and not looked at how it works.
Write a technical description of about 1,200 words of how the Raft consensus algorithm elects a leader. The reader is a backend engineer.
Write a technical description of about 300 words of how regenerative braking works in an electric car. The reader is a driver with no engineering background.
